judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's catch-all keys are computed from z.string().toString() (which does not produce a wildcard/passthrough key), so unknown properties like refresh_token are stripped from the parsed output, and the function then writes the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token, which callers persist to the credential record. The first credential-sync refresh overwrites the user's real OAuth refresh token in the DB with the placeholder string "refresh_token"; every subsequent real-provider refresh fails permanently, silently breaking the user's calendar/video integration until manual re-auth. Callers (GoogleCalendarService.ts, Office365CalendarService.ts, zoom VideoApiAdapter.ts) all write the returned object straight into prisma.credential.update.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to allow arbitrary keys via computed properties `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, but those evaluate to a *literal string key* and do not make the schema passthrough/catchall. Zod `z.object(...)` will therefore strip unknown properties like `refresh_token`. The function then forces `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing. Call sites then persist/propagate this parsed result: e.g. `Office365CalendarService.ts` merges `tokenResponse.data` back into `o365AuthCredentials`, overwriting the real stored refresh token with the placeholder; `GoogleCalendarService.ts` stores the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` directly into Prisma `credential.update({ data: { key } })`, also risking persisting the placeholder. This can permanently break subsequent token refreshes when credential sync mode is enabled.
